review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the uses of the entry and val lemmas. The file has no @[simp] attributes, so I found no loops or competing rules. The problems are in the interface itself. The matrix-entry lemmas for the private GL2 elements are all rfl, but they are not registered with simp. Use sites either list them by hand or unfold the definitions. I did not run Lean, so the effect of tagging them is untested.

findings.declaration: tri₂_apply₀₀ … diag₂_apply₁₁ (entry lemmas for tri₂, tri₂⁻¹ and diag₂)
findings.problem: Twelve rfl entry lemmas for tri₂, tri₂⁻¹ and diag₂ are not tagged @[simp]. Each use re-lists them by hand. Lines 535-561 use `simp only [... tri₂_apply₀₀, tri₂_apply₁₀, tri₂_inv_apply₁₀ ...]`. Lines 658 and 695 list the four diag₂ entry lemmas, and line 743 uses an rw chain. Plain simp cannot compute entries of these elements. Several proofs therefore unfold the definition with `simp [diag₂]` (lines 194, 203, 209) or `simp [tri₂]` (line 495), instead of using one canonical entry normal form. diag₂_val and unip₂_val (lines 187-191) are only used with rw. There is no tri₂_val.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the entry lemmas @[simp], along with diag₂_val and unip₂_val, and add a tri₂_val. Each rewrite turns Units.val of a constructor-built element into an entry or an explicit matrix, so it makes the term smaller and should not loop. Then shorten the hand-maintained simp only lists, and replace `simp [diag₂]` unfoldings by plain `simp`. Test whether the extra simp lemmas interfere with `Matrix.mul_apply` and `Fin.sum_univ_two` in lines 535-561 before committing to this.
findings.benefit: The same entry facts would be stated once instead of repeated in each proof. Proofs would stop depending on the internal definition of diag₂, tri₂ and unip₂. If a definition changed, only the entry lemmas would need updating.

findings.declaration: unip₂_mul_weyl₂_apply_zero_zero / lunip₂_apply_zero_zero and the membership lemmas for unip₂, diag₂, weyl₂, lunip₂
findings.problem: The simp interface for unip₂, lunip₂ and weyl₂ is incomplete. Entries such as `unip₂_mul_weyl₂_apply_zero_zero` and `lunip₂_apply_one_zero` are proved by unfolding the definitions (`simp [unip₂, weyl₂]`). They are not simp lemmas, and unip₂, lunip₂ and weyl₂ have no val/entry lemmas at all, although unip₂ has unip₂_val. Each membership proof (lines 221-252) repeats `fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp [def, Units.inv_mk, ...]`, which unfolds the definition and also depends on the inv field and on `Units.inv_mk`. The entries of products such as unip₂ t * weyl₂ are not covered by any simp rule, so a one-off lemma is needed (lines 254-260).
findings.proposed_change: Add simp lemmas for the val and inv entries of unip₂, lunip₂ and weyl₂, for example by stating `lunip₂_val` and `weyl₂_val` in the same way as `unip₂_val`. Then these proofs can run with plain `simp` using `Matrix.mul_apply`, `Fin.sum_univ_two` and the entry lemmas. Where one-off lemmas such as `lunip₂_apply_zero_zero` remain, tag them @[simp] and drop the explicit unfolding.
findings.benefit: The membership and entry proofs would no longer depend on how the structures are defined. The one-off product-entry lemmas could disappear, and new facts about these elements would be easier to add.
